input: Draft a script for a short animated explainer

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The topic or subject being explained is the entire foundation of the script — without it, nothing can be written.
Knowing who the audience is determines the vocabulary, assumed knowledge level, and how concepts are framed.
The target duration directly controls how much content, how many scenes, and how deep the explanation can go.
Where the video will be published or shown (e.g. website, social media, investor pitch, classroom) shapes pacing, length, and tone.
Tone and style (e.g. playful vs. professional, humorous vs. serious) define the voice, character design cues, and narrative approach.
The core action or feeling the viewer should take away determines what the script must build toward and how it ends.
Knowing the script format expected (e.g. voiceover-only, dialogue, scene directions included) determines how the document should be structured.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a short animated explainer script
gold.taskDescription: Write a script for a short animated explainer video covering a specific topic for a defined audience.

questions.title: What specific topic or product is being explained?
questions.description: Identify the exact subject matter the animated explainer will cover.

questions.title: Who is the target audience for this video?
questions.description: Define the intended viewers — their background, familiarity with the topic, and demographics.

questions.title: How long should the finished video be?
questions.description: Establish the target runtime to calibrate word count, scene count, and depth of explanation.

questions.title: Where will this video be published or screened?
questions.description: Determine the platform or setting — website, social media, pitch deck, classroom, etc.

questions.title: What tone should the script strike — playful, professional, or other?
questions.description: Clarify the desired voice and style so the writing matches the brand or intent.

questions.title: What should viewers think, feel, or do after watching?
questions.description: Identify the single most important takeaway or call to action the script must deliver.

questions.title: Should the script include scene directions and visual cues?
questions.description: Decide whether the output is voiceover text only or a full production script with on-screen action notes.
